title: Run it end to end
summary: Start the three tiers in the right order, test the API alone, and fix a CORS error.

quiz.q: Put the start-up steps in the best order.
lines: Check the API with curl or the browser
quiz.explain: Each tier needs the one below it. Checking the API before Angular tells you which tier is faulty if something fails.

quiz.q: The Angular page shows a CORS error but `curl http://localhost:3000/students` returns JSON. Where do you fix it?
options: In the Express server, by allowing the Angular origin
quiz.explain: CORS is a permission the server gives to a browser origin. curl ignores it, which is why curl works while the page fails.

quiz.q: Which of these is a different origin from `http://localhost:4200`?
quiz.explain: An origin is the protocol, host and port together. Only the port differs in `localhost:3000`, and that is enough.

quiz.q: Complete the command that serves an Angular project during development.
quiz.explain: `ng serve` builds the app, serves it on port 4200 and reloads when you save a file.

quiz.q: The API prints a connection refused error for port 27017. What is the most likely cause?
quiz.explain: 27017 is MongoDB's default port. Refused means nothing is listening there, so start `mongod`.
